newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to allow pension money use in investments.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to allow pension money use in investments.

text.p: Eligible contributors to the Malaysian pension fund will be allowed to withdraw part of their money to invest in approved units trusts from November 1, the national Bernama news agency reported on Friday.
It quoted Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) executive chairman, Sallehuddin Mohamed, as saying that about 120,000 contributors below 55 years old would be eligible for the scheme.
The scheme would help to expand the local capital market and develop the fund management industry, he told a news conference.
Under the scheme, contributors will be allowed to withdraw 20 percent of excess EPF funds above 50,000 ringgit.
Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim recently announced the plan to allow the EPF withdrawals as part of efforts to liberalise the country's capital market.
The government last month launched a unit trust fund for young Malaysians open to all races. It runs a number of other unit trust funds open to Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) investors.

Sallehuddin said fund management institutions eligible to take part include state investment agency Permodalan Nasional Bhd, pilgrimage fund board Tabung Haji, unit trust companies approved by the Securities Commission and local fund management companies licensed under the Securities Industry Act (SIA).
Merchant banks which undertake fund management and are licensed under the Banking and Finance Institutions Act and SIA are also eligible.
